title: Request for Larger Cabin Window Apertures in the Upper Deck Rear Cabin
abstract: Verdant Isles Airways asked for larger cabin windows in the rear upper deck to support a premium product refresh. The request was closed without a modification after the structural consequences were assessed.

sections.request: We are refreshing the upper deck product and the design agency have come back with a cabin concept built around a larger window. The feedback from our premium passengers is consistently that the upper deck feels enclosed compared with what our competitors offer on their newer aircraft, and the window size is the thing they mention. We would like to know what it would take to open up the aperture in the rear part of the upper deck cabin, say from the mid galley aft, and whether it can be done at the same time as the cabin reconfiguration we already have planned. We are not asking for every window, only the rows where our new suites sit. If the whole aperture cannot change we would be interested in anything that makes the window look larger from inside the cabin.
sections.background: Our upper deck product scores well on seat and service and poorly on cabin feel. The reconfiguration is already funded and the aircraft are due through the shop between 2027 and 2029. We raised a similar question informally two years ago and were told it was difficult, but the cabin design has moved on since then and we would like a formal answer we can show our board.
sections.expected_outcome: Either a modification that enlarges the aperture in the rear upper deck cabin, embodied during the planned reconfiguration, or a clear statement of why it cannot be done together with any alternative that improves the perceived window size from inside the cabin.

type_data.business_justification: Premium cabin refresh scoring poorly on perceived cabin space, with window size the most frequently cited factor in passenger feedback.
type_data.closure_note: No modification will be raised. The upper deck window aperture is cut through a stringer bay whose pitch is set by the frame spacing, and enlarging it requires a new cut-out reinforcement, a new frame and a re-substantiation of the pressurised shell in that bay for the full fatigue life. The change is a major structural redesign of the rear upper deck rather than a cabin change, and it cannot be embodied inside a reconfiguration slot. A cabin trim option that increases the visible aperture by widening the reveal without touching the structure has been offered instead, and the operator has been put in contact with the cabin definition office to price it.
